newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index gains on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index gains on foreign demand.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index gained a further 27.34 points on Thursday to 3499.37 on heavy foreign buying, brokers said.
This was the fourth consecutive gain for the index this week prompted by a majority foreign demand.
Turnover was posted at 36.039 million shillings on 696,477 shares from 21.484 million on 525,207 shares on Wednesday.
Foreign investors traded 100,000 of Firestone East Africa at a reserved price of 33 from 30 and 102,000 shares of Uchumi Supermarket at 41.50 from 37.50, all on the three-day special board.
Bourse officials said despite the increased activity from foreigners, the majority of investors -- notably institutional mainly long-term investors -- were keeping a wary eye on the market.
"They are still cautious, trading with a definite wait-and-see attitude especially as they wait for the financial year-end results," an official said.

Brokers said that the market maxim "investors buy on a rumour -- sell on the fact" also held true for the NSE at the moment. Speculators were now buying heavily in the financials as rumours of bonus shares with positive year-end results flood the market, they added.
Standard Chartered traded at 65.50 from 56 while Barclays Bank of Kenya traded 48,000 shares at a reserve price of 123 from 116 on the one-hour special board.
Kenya Commercial Bank was unchanged at 90 while National Bank of Kenya edged to 15.90 from 15.50.
Foreigners in national carrier Kenya Airways sold some 5,000 shares at 9.0 from 8.70 to local investors.
British American Tobacco Kenya eased to 75.50 from 79 while Rea Vipingo Plantations rose to 11.50 from 11.25.
